To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) The spin and the parity of a new resonance produced singly at the LHC can be determined by studying its angular and mass distributions in the decay to gauge boson pairs.

the spin of the new bosons can be determined with a confidence level (CL) of 99% by studying angular and/or mass distributions in the decays $X \to ZZ, WW, \gamma \gamma \to 4 f$, and that the CL of the spin determination is improved by studying the angular distributions in the decaying boson subsystems $VV \to 4\ell, 2\ell2\gamma, 4\gamma$.
• We have developed a complete Monte Carlo simulation for the process pp → X → VV → 4f at the LHC, which is valid for any spin J of the resonance X and includes all possible spin correlations.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of new techniques for the experimental determination of the spin, parity and tensor structure of couplings of the new bosons to Standard Model particles by studying angular and invariant mass distributions of events with the decay of the bosons to pairs of gauge and Higgs bosons.
the study of the angular distribution of the decay products of a new particle produced at the LHC in association with the Higgs boson.
the study of the properties of new boson discovered at the LHC in terms of its spin, parity, tensor structure, and the possibility of its decay to two photons.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we show how the spin of a new particle can be determined at a hadron collider by measuring its angular and mass distribution in its decay products.
the angular distribution of the decay products of the new resonance can be used to determine the spin of the resonance and the parity of the resonance with a confidence level greater than 95%.

it is possible to distinguish between the spin 0 hypothesis and spin 2 hypothesis at 99% confidence level with 8 TeV LHC data, and that it is possible for the spin 2 hypothesis to be distinguished from the spin 2 with non-parity eigenstate hypothesis with 14 TeV LHC.

, by the end of 8 TeV LHC run, the spin and parity can be determined with a high confidence level for a wide range models.
